title: Modi Naturals Ltd - 519003 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Modi Naturals Q4 FY26 revenue rose 28% to INR243 crore and PAT 141% to INR19.7 crore, with FY26 PAT up 62.1% to INR50.3 crore.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to INR243 crore, EBITDA rose 51.8% to INR24.5 crore (10.1% margin) and PAT rose 141% to INR19.7 crore. For FY26, revenue grew 8.5% to INR719 crore, EBITDA grew 31.2% to INR73.5 crore (10.2% margin, excluding exceptional item) and PAT grew 62.1% to INR50.3 crore. Management said the expanded ethanol plant (282 KLPD, up from 130 KL) started commercial operations late in the year, so its contribution was limited in FY26 and is expected to build from FY27. Growth in the consumer and bulk businesses was mixed, with the consumer segment flat for the year and the bulk segment up sharply.

financial_highlights.metric: Insurance claim received in Q4 FY26 (business interruption, FY24 ethanol breakdown)

segments.name: Consumer division
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR50.9 crore (vs INR48.5 crore) and EBITDA INR4.2 crore (vs INR3 crore); FY26 revenue INR183.5 crore (vs INR179.4 crore, about 2% growth) and EBITDA INR15.2 crore (vs INR15.1 crore). Management cited the margin at about 8.3% for the division.

segments.name: Bulk division
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR100 crore (vs INR56.1 crore) and EBITDA INR2.7 crore (vs INR0.9 lakh); FY26 revenue INR198.3 crore (vs INR158.6 crore) and EBITDA INR2.6 crore (vs INR1.7 crore). One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit was shut for non-viability.

segments.name: Ethanol division
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 revenue INR92.2 crore and EBITDA INR18.5 crore (about 18.8% margin, including an exceptional item); FY26 revenue INR337.4 crore and EBITDA INR58.2 crore (about 17% margin). Management guides about INR950 crore average revenue for FY27 and a sustainable 12-15% EBITDA margin.

guidance_outlook: Ethanol FY27 revenue guidance of an average INR950 crore, which management called conservative; it assumes only about 50% utilisation of the expanded capacity.
Management said consolidated revenue would cross INR1,100 crore at full utilisation of ethanol capacity.
Long-term sustainable ethanol EBITDA margin guided at 12-15%, with some quarters above that range.
Medium-term ambition for the FMCG business of INR500 crore: about INR300-350 crore from oils and INR150 crore from food.
No large capex planned for FY27 beyond up to INR20 crore for a by-product value-addition project in ethanol.
Management expects the expanded ethanol facility's benefits to become more visible from FY27 as utilisation improves.
capex_capacity: Phase 2 of the ethanol expansion was commissioned, taking capacity from 130 KLPD to 282 KLPD; commercial operations began in the latter part of FY26.

Ethanol order from PSU OMCs in cycle one of ESY 2025-26 (till 31 October 2026) is 47.9 crore litres (47.9 kilo KL as stated), about 150 KLPD at 330 operating days; management said it chose not to bid for private OMC tenders earlier because the plant was not ready.
Up to INR20 crore planned for a value-addition project in the ethanol by-product stream; no other large capex this financial year.
One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit shut down due to non-viability.
summary.management_tone: Confident and forward-looking on ethanol demand and FY27 guidance, while being evasive on export policy, licensing and acquisition details ("nothing firmed up yet"). Management was specific about financial results but gave limited breakdowns of the consumer brand and margin mix.
key_quotes: So it's purely the risk ofexecution, nothing else.
And of course, from 1st November, we will be rebidding for the next cycle.
I think with full capacity utilization, our consolidated revenue will cross INR1,100 crores.

qa_highlights.question: What are the risks in ethanol and consumer over the next six to eight quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Ethanol risk is overcapacity and underutilisation, which management said it is well placed to handle given expansion and tailwinds such as higher blending. Consumer risk is purely execution, given brands and new product lineups.

qa_highlights.question: Is an acquisition in the food sector close?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a few food-sector opportunities were evaluated but nothing is firmed up yet; it will update when there is progress.

qa_highlights.question: Will ethanol value-addition revenue show up by end FY27 or early FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said one by-product value-added innovation is already helping EBITDA margins and a second is underway, to be completed in a few months; alcohol-side options include potable (RS/ENA, bottling) and downstream chemicals, with little detail shared.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is the company of using 282 KLPD, and how long does the PSU OMC order run?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited headroom in consumption and plant location, and said the order covers the ongoing ESY cycle one only, to 31 October 2026, with private OMC registration and tenders expected to add volume.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ethanol EBITDA margin rise to about 17% from 13% when revenue guidance is INR950 crore, and what is sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said grain prices softened and by-product value addition helped, and Q4 included an exceptional item lifting margin to 18.8%. Long-term sustainable margin remains 12-15%, with some quarters above that; INR950 crore guidance assumes about 50% utilisation of the expansion.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth outlook for the consumer division?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 growth was about 2% but Q4 grew faster and momentum is built, so growth is expected to accelerate; drivers are olive oil, pasta, hing and new launches later this year.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the segment EBITDA differ from the P&L EBITDA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the difference is netting off of inter-division interest in consolidated results, which is not reflected in segment results.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak ethanol revenue at full utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said consolidated revenue would cross INR1,100 crore at full capacity utilisation.

demand_pricing: Consumer division: Q4 FY26 revenue INR50.9 crore (vs INR48.5 crore) and FY26 INR183.5 crore (vs INR179.4 crore, about 2% growth); management said demand is improving on expanded distribution, innovation and new launches.

Consumer channel mix: about 50% modern trade, 40% general trade and 8-10% army/CSD; general trade covers about 50,000 outlets directly, with presence in about 25 of them. Food products are roughly 10% of consumer sales and edible oils roughly 90%.
Consumer margin: division EBITDA margin about 8.3%; management said food categories are profitable from year one or two and no loss-making categories are pursued.

Bulk division: Q4 FY26 revenue INR100 crore (vs INR56.1 crore) and FY26 INR198.3 crore (vs INR158.6 crore); Q4 EBITDA INR2.7 crore vs INR0.9 lakh a year earlier. One solvent extraction plant in Pilibhit shut for non-viability.

Ethanol demand: PSU OMC cycle-one order for ESY 2025-26 (to 31 October 2026) is 47.9 crore litres, about 150 KLPD at 330 operating days, versus 130 KLPD earlier. Management said PSU OMCs are about 90% of the market and private OMCs about 10%; fresh tenders expected by end-June 2026. Rebidding for next cycle from 1 November, in September-October.
risks_watch: Ethanol overcapacity and underutilisation across the industry, with management saying the surge in capacity happened over the last three years; watch PSU OMC and private OMC tender volumes from end-June 2026 and the 1 November rebid.
Export policy for 1G ethanol and whether the expanded plants will be authorised for exports; management declined to speculate and said policy would come over the next few weeks.
Ethanol margin sustainability: Q4 included an exceptional item and softer grain prices; management guides 12-15% long-term, versus about 17% for FY26.
Consumer execution risk and growth reacceleration after about 2% FY26 revenue growth; monitor Q1 FY27 consumer revenue against Q4 FY26 INR50.9 crore.
Pending food-sector acquisition: management said nothing is firmed up yet, so timing and size are unknown.
Auditor transition: management said the change was a planned succession, but the resignation was reported recently; monitor the new auditor's appointment and any further disclosures.

adds.what: Ethanol plant Phase 2 expansion, capacity 130 KLPD to 282 KLPD (commissioned, commercial operations began late FY26)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 ethanol revenue of about INR950 crore (vs INR337 crore in FY26) and consolidated revenue above INR1,100 crore at full utilisation, backed by the commissioned 282 KLPD ethanol plant and a PSU OMC order of 47.9 crore litres (~150 KLPD) for ESY 2025-26, though the brief gives no explicit FY27 consolidated growth figure and assumes only 50% utilisation.
